evidence: Read CONTEXT whole first: heading 'When the adult role is not available yet', a problem paragraph that ends on the baby-bird line, then the draft as the whole second paragraph (it appears once, exactly as in DRAFT.txt), then the steps. Draft judged: 'So, I came up with the idea of constructing a bridge - a temporary fix - a borrowed adulthood, if I can put it that way. It's made up of a number of familiar practices (such as modeling and supported action), even though I'm not claiming the whole sequence has been proven as one treatment.' VOICE AND SEAM: the 'So,' follows the baby-bird punchline the way speech would, and the register matches the neighbouring casual lines ('like telling a baby bird to just fly', 'a cup of sugar from a neighbor'); the second sentence is a little more formal, but it is about the evidential status of his own method and the paragraph above it is already clinical ('adult functions', 'child part'), so I felt no seam. 'Even though' reads coherently (not claiming proof would lead you to expect untested novelty; it is made of familiar practices anyway), so it is a loose concessive, not a logic slip. AGAINST SOURCE: it keeps the provisional bridge (temporary fix), his authorship (I came up with the idea), the name borrowed adulthood (the aside marks it as his own coinage), the familiar practices with the same two examples the replaced words gave (the longer witnessing/modeling/supported action/gradual transfer list in the meaning-to-keep line is not claimed to be complete because of 'such as', and the replaced words also named only two), and the no-proof caveat (not claiming the whole sequence proven as one treatment). It does what the_change says: both published points are in. It adds no practice, study, number or personal fact; 'a number of' is padding only. TELLS: I checked T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the literal draft in context and found none PRESENT. Borderlines I looked at and cleared: T07 (the 'if I can put it that way' aside attaches to a real thought-turn, the slightly odd coined phrase 'borrowed adulthood', and it sits inside a sentence, not as a stage direction between beats); T03 (the no-proof caveat is prepared by the sentence that introduces his own invented method, in a guide full of safety cautions); T15 (the swaps from the source are plain, equally likely words such as made up of, claiming, such as, not exotic synonyms); T19 (the first sentence introduces the bridge but carries his coinage, so it is not a pure announcement); T21 (the caveat sentence has two jobs, as the source sentence did, joined by one concession, not a coordinated list of jobs); T26 (adulthood and borrow recur as the section's deliberate metaphor, forced adulthood against borrowed adulthood); T29 (the last sentence is a new consideration, not a restatement); C02 ('the whole sequence' looks forward to the steps below exactly as the source sentence did); C03 ('came up with the idea' is the same fact as his published 'author-developed'). The spaced en dashes are the one punctuation habit not seen elsewhere in this section; no tell row covers dashes and the chain bridge / temporary fix / borrowed adulthood is renaming in speech, not a staged reveal, so I did not count it as a seam. LINTER: 'B1 finished principle' flagged the second sentence; the context answers it, because it is a specific caveat about his own bridge, long and qualified rather than compressed, restores a published point, and is not a general aphorism or a clever closer. 'D9 follows the source order' is trivially true of a one-paragraph, two-sentence replacement; I checked T13 (the aside and the concession are small noticings) and T09 (no equal-weight run) and found neither. Small note: the writer's D9 reason lists 'of course', 'just' and '!', which are not in this draft; the only Emulate aside here is 'if I can put it that way', and that does not change the judgment.
